name: Standing adversarial self-review
claim_class: A claim that a build step is finished and ready to hand off, before any reviewer has looked at it.
proof_obligation: Every build prompt includes a self-review section the agent runs against its own output before handoff, with each item applied where it is relevant to the change. It answers the questions an outside reviewer would ask, before they get asked, and it raises the floor for everything that follows. The checklist: list every error variant the step can produce, and for each one record its route, whether it is retried or treated as terminal on the first occurrence, and whether the failure is transient or deterministic, presented as a table with a correctness column; flag any transient failure routed to a terminal path, which throws away work that could have been recovered, and any deterministic failure routed to a retry path, which repeats a loop that can never succeed. Any value meant to be checked against a real or measured value needs a test where the two values differ, not just one where they already match, because a check only ever run against equal values has never exercised the correction it exists to perform. Any lock must be checked for re-entrancy across calls that could re-enter the same lock, including through a logging or tracing call whose sink takes the same lock. Every filesystem operation states whether its containment check resolves the real path and confirms it sits inside the owned root, or whether it only inspects the path string for parent-directory segments; the string-only check is wrong because a path can look contained while a symlink points it somewhere else, and containment has to cover reads, writes, and deletes alike. Finally, the review names any assumption that is relied on but never checked in code, any window where state can change between a check and the use of that check, and any acceptance claim asserted in the report without a test that proves it. The step also confirms the existing test suite still passes, the build produces no warnings, and its own headline acceptance criterion is proven by a test that would fail if that criterion were not met.
failure_mode: Without a standing self-review, the questions an independent reviewer would ask go unasked until a later, more expensive review catches them, if it catches them at all: a transient error wired to a terminal path silently discards recoverable work, a deterministic error wired to a retry path spins forever, a reconciliation check tested only against matching values passes even though its comparison logic is broken, a lock taken around a logging call deadlocks the first time that call re-enters it, and a path check that only looks at the string lets a symlink write or delete somewhere outside the directory it was supposed to be confined to. An assumed invariant, an unguarded check-then-use window, or an acceptance claim asserted without a proving test reads as a correct-looking checkmark sitting over a claim nobody actually verified.
origin_incident: No single recorded event is documented for this rule. It generalizes a recurring pattern instead: without a standing checklist, each of these defects, misrouted transient and deterministic failures, an always-agreeing reconciliation test, a re-entrant lock, a path check that only inspects the string, an unproven acceptance claim, has shown up in delivered work whose own report described it as complete.
